verdict.rationale: Open WebUI is itself an AI assistant platform. Its docs describe an agentic mode where models autonomously search and follow links, a delegate_task tool that hands work to parallel sub-agents with tool access, and per-chat tool approval modes for supervising delegated work. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of delegation quality, and clarity on how much of the sub-agent and supervision capability lives in the separate 'Computer' ecosystem component versus core Open WebUI, which also depends on a user-supplied model.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: The AI can delegate work to parallel sub-agents with the delegate_task tool. Each sub-agent is a full chat with tool access
By enabling Native Function Calling (Agentic Mode), you allow quality models to independently explore the web, verify facts, and follow links autonomously.
Every chat has a tool approval mode, set from the + menu in the chat input
You see the full history: every file it read, every edit it made, and the pending approval that's blocking it, rendered as tool cards with Allow / Deny buttons.
